item.title: China Coast Guard Hosts High-Level Meeting of the 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies Meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) successfully hosted the High-Level Meeting of the 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies Meeting (HACGAM) in Hangzhou City, east China's Zhejiang Province, from September 7 to 10, 2026. A total of 124 representatives attended the meeting, including delegates from maritime law enforcement agencies of 23 countries and regions — such as the Republic of Korea, Singapore, and Vietnam — as well as two international organizations: the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Piracy and Armed Robbery against Ships in Asia - Information Sharing Centre (ReCAAPISC). During the meeting, the participants conducted in-depth and pragmatic discussions on such key topics as the regional maritime security situation, prevention and combating of transnational maritime crime, maritime search and rescue cooperation, marine environmental protection, law enforcement information-sharing mechanisms, and law enforcement capacity building. The parties reached preliminary consensus on the cooperation plan for the next phase and issued the Joint Statement of the 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies Meeting. At the conclusion of the meeting, the China Coast Guard handed over the meeting flag to the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency, the host of the next meeting.

item.title: China lodges solemn representations with Italy, EU over DPP official's visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China has lodged solemn representations with Italy and the EU over the visit of "Taiwan independence" politicians to Italy for a conference, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Friday. Mao made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked to comment on Taiwan's Hsiao Bi-khim's visit to Italy. "The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities and certain politicians are resorting to all manner of tricks to seek publicity," Mao said. Noting that they seek independence by colluding with external forces under the pretext of "democracy" and "freedom," Mao said such acts are contemptible and will ultimately prove futile. Mao stressed that there is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory. China has always firmly opposed any form of official exchanges between countries that have established diplomatic ties with China and China's Taiwan region, Mao said. Mao said the one‑China principle is a universally recognized norm in international relations and the common consensus of the international community. It also constitutes the political foundation of China‑Italy relations and China‑EU relations, she added. "We urge the relevant parties to honour the one‑China principle with concrete actions," the spokesperson said.

item.title: Xi urges efforts to prevent major accidents after cargo ship fire in east China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged resolute efforts to prevent major accidents after a foreign cargo ship caught fire in east China's Shandong Province. The cargo ship caught fire on Thursday morning while undergoing repairs at a port in the city of Qingdao, Shandong, causing major casualties. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called for intensified efforts to search and rescue people who are missing and provide support for those affected. In his instructions, he demanded efforts to promptly determine the cause of the accident and hold those responsible accountable. Xi also required local governments and related departments to draw lessons from the accident, thoroughly identify and address fire hazards, ensure the effective implementation of preventive measures, resolutely prevent major accidents, and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang called for immediate search and rescue operations for the trapped people, as well as full efforts to treat the injured, properly handle follow-up work, and guard against secondary disasters. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, urged the Work Safety Commission under the State Council to thoroughly identify workplace safety risks and take concrete steps to prevent major accidents. The Ministry of Emergency Management has dispatched a work team to the site to guide rescue efforts, while the provincial authorities of Shandong have mobilized resources to carry out on-site response efforts.

item.title: Taiwan has never been a country and will never be one: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Tuesday that Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country, adding that the Lai Ching-te authorities' deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for "Taiwan independence." Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on Lai's claim that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758 and that Taiwan is a "sovereign independent nation." Lai Ching-te authorities' rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community's steadfast commitment to one China, she said. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which "decides to restore all its rights to the People's Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations," she said. From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN, she said, adding that it made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as "two Chinas" or "one China, one Taiwan."
